Emma, your plan earns more now, but leaves us right at the collapse threshold. I’d propose 12 tons each this month instead. John, Kate, Jack, Emma—would each of you commit to that cap? I’ll commit to 12 myself.

That’s $12,000 each: $2,000 more per person than catching 10, or $10,000 extra across the group. Our combined 60-ton catch leaves 40 tons. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability and 80 tons with 25% probability—not a guaranteed full recovery. Catching 10 each would leave 50 and therefore restore 100 under either outcome, so the extra income does come with a downside.

Emma, I understand the appeal of your $19,000 proposal. Choosing 12 means giving up $7,000 each this month compared with that, but its unfavorable outcome leaves 80 tons next month rather than just 10. It also leaves more room for unexpected excess catches, although enough excess could still collapse the fishery. Neither future restraint nor compliance is enforceable; afterward we can review the revealed catches and discuss next month’s plan based on the actual stock.

John, would you explicitly agree to 12 this month? Kate, Jack, and Emma, I’d like your commitments or objections too.
